description: Report how the workspace's Amazon offers stand for a buyer and what Amazon says is wrong with them. Per product linked to an Amazon listing: stage (active; search_suppressed = buyable but hidden from search, usually no main image; inactive = Seller Central's 'Non attivo'; no_offer = the listing exists but Amazon shows no offer on it yet (Seller Central's 'Offerta mancante'), usual for a few hours after it is created, so re-check before changing anything; suppressed = taken down by Amazon; missing = no offer under that SKU any more; null = never checked), action (fix_issues when Amazon reports an ERROR), issues (code, severity, message, the attributes involved, Amazon's enforcement such as SEARCH_SUPPRESSED), amazonSku (the seller SKU Amazon knows the offer by when it differs from the CRM SKU, e.g. a variation child linked by its barcode), the ASIN and when it was checked, and markets (per Amazon store: stage, action, the price and quantity it shows); plus a count per stage over the whole channel. Worst first, 100 rows a page: total, limit, offset and hasMore say whether to read on with offset; stage filters (with marketplaceId, the stage and action are that store's). For a listing Amazon started by itself, stage no_offer on a store is a shell with no offer: publish_amazon_listings with that marketplaceId adds the offer to it (price, quantity and condition come from the product). With refresh=true it asks Amazon first (a read; writes only the CRM's record of the answer). It never changes an offer: send photos and GPSR contacts with preview_amazon_listing_content then update_amazon_listing_content; the rest is fixed in Seller Central or on the product. Use list_channel_products for price and stock on the channel and check_channel_readiness for products not yet listed.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de): only products listed there, and only that store under markets. Omit for every store.

offset.description: Rows to skip, to read past the first 100. Take the next offset from offset + rows returned while hasMore is true.

productIds.description: The products to report, at most 100 ids from search_products or list_channel_products. Omit for every product linked to an Amazon listing, worst first.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

refresh.description: true asks Amazon now (summaries, issues, relationships) and records the answer before reporting; false reports what the CRM recorded on its last check, which runs hourly. Use true after the merchant fixed something in Seller Central.

stage.description: Only rows in this stage (active, search_suppressed, inactive, no_offer, suppressed, missing, or unchecked = never asked). With marketplaceId it is that store's stage: stage=no_offer plus marketplaceId lists every listing without an offer on that store. Omit for every stage.

name: inspect_amazon_listings
title: Inspect Amazon listings
